items.followUp: What is the least count of a vernier callipers with 10 vernier divisions equal to 9 main-scale divisions, if 1 main-scale division is 1 mm?

rubric.why: Award for identifying what a vernier callipers is used to measure.
rubric.description: Defines vernier callipers as an instrument for precise measurement.
rubric.how: State that it measures small lengths or dimensions, such as internal or external diameter, accurately.

rubric.why: The least count is the difference between one main-scale division and one vernier-scale division; its common value is 0.1 mm.
rubric.description: Gives the least-count relation and/or its usual value.
rubric.how: Write L.C. = 1 MSD − 1 VSD = 0.1 mm (0.01 cm).

modelAnswer: Vernier callipers is an instrument used to measure small lengths and dimensions, such as internal or external diameters, accurately.
Least count (L.C.) = 1 main-scale division − 1 vernier-scale division = 0.1 mm = 0.01 cm.

items.followUp: What are significant figures? State the number of significant figures in 0.00450 m.

rubric.why: Significant figures include the accurately known digits of a measurement.
rubric.description: Identifies the certain or accurately known digits.
rubric.how: State that significant figures include all digits known with certainty.

rubric.why: The first doubtful or uncertain digit is also included.
rubric.description: Includes the first uncertain digit in the definition.
rubric.how: State that the first doubtful (uncertain) digit is included.

modelAnswer: The significant figures of a measurement are all the digits known with certainty, together with the first doubtful or uncertain digit.

items.followUp: Define translatory motion and rotational motion.

rubric.why: Linear motion is motion along a straight path.
rubric.how: State that an object moves along a straight line.

rubric.why: Circular motion follows a circular path.
rubric.how: State that an object moves along a circular path.

modelAnswer: Linear motion is the motion of an object along a straight line.
Circular motion is the motion of an object along a circular path.

items.followUp: Differentiate between distance and displacement, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: A scalar has magnitude only; mass and time are examples.
rubric.description: Defines a scalar and gives an example.
rubric.how: State that a scalar has magnitude only and name a scalar quantity.

rubric.why: A vector has both magnitude and direction; force and velocity are examples.
rubric.description: Defines a vector and gives an example.
rubric.how: State that a vector has magnitude and direction and name a vector quantity.

modelAnswer: A scalar quantity has magnitude only; for example, mass.
A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction; for example, force.

items.followUp: State Newton’s first law of motion and explain how it illustrates inertia.

rubric.why: The law states that a body retains its state of rest or uniform straight-line motion.
rubric.description: States the body's unchanged state of motion.
rubric.how: Mention that a body remains at rest or continues in uniform straight-line motion.

rubric.why: A change occurs only when an unbalanced external force acts.
rubric.description: States the condition for changing the body's state.
rubric.how: Mention that an unbalanced external force is required to change its state.

modelAnswer: A body remains at rest, or continues to move with uniform velocity in a straight line, unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force.
This tendency of a body to resist a change in its state of motion is called inertia.

items.followUp: Write two differences between distance and displacement.

rubric.why: Mass is the amount of matter in a body, whereas weight is the gravitational force acting on it.
rubric.description: Distinguishes mass and weight by their meanings.
rubric.how: State that mass measures matter and weight is gravitational force.

rubric.why: Mass is measured in kilograms and is constant for a body; weight is measured in newtons and varies with gravitational field strength.
rubric.description: Gives a further difference, such as units or dependence on gravity.
rubric.how: Compare their SI units or state that weight depends on g while mass remains constant.

modelAnswer: Mass is the amount of matter in a body, whereas weight is the gravitational force acting on the body.
Mass is measured in kilograms and remains constant; weight is measured in newtons and depends on the value of gravitational acceleration, g.

items.followUp: Describe two methods used to increase friction between surfaces.

rubric.description: Names lubrication as a method of reducing friction.
rubric.how: State that applying oil or grease between surfaces reduces friction.

rubric.why: Smoothing surfaces or using rolling elements can reduce friction.
rubric.description: Names another valid method of reducing friction.
rubric.how: Give a second method, such as polishing surfaces or using ball bearings.

modelAnswer: Apply a lubricant, such as oil or grease, between the surfaces.
Use ball bearings or rollers to reduce sliding friction by replacing it with rolling friction.

items.followUp: What is the resultant of two perpendicular forces of 3 N and 4 N?

rubric.why: A resultant is one force that represents the combined forces.
rubric.description: Identifies the resultant as a single equivalent force.
rubric.how: State that the resultant is a single force.

rubric.why: The resultant produces the same effect as all the forces acting together.
rubric.description: States the equivalence to the combined action of the forces.
rubric.how: Explain that it has the same effect as the original forces acting together.

modelAnswer: The resultant of a system of forces is the single force that produces the same effect as all the forces acting together.
